what: FedEx delivers packages and freight worldwide. It runs an air network built around its Memphis hub for express delivery, a ground network for cheaper parcels, and a freight business for pallet-sized shipments that it is separating.
customers: Businesses shipping goods, e-commerce retailers, healthcare companies and consumers in more than 220 countries.
money: express air, ground and international delivery, now combined into one network
less-than-truckload freight, to be spun off as a separate company
moat: An air fleet, hubs and sorting network that cost decades and tens of billions to build, with the express network uniquely able to move urgent shipments overnight.
risks: Industrial freight demand has been weak for several years
Fuel costs and aircraft maintenance are large and variable
The end of low-value import duty exemptions reduced a profitable flow of small parcels
Separating FedEx Freight removes a high-margin business
opportunities: Combining the express and ground networks is cutting billions of fixed costs
Spinning off Freight may let the market value both parts more highly
Higher-value healthcare and international shipments improve the revenue mix
watch: Cost savings delivered from the network consolidation and average revenue per package.
